_field_definitions.db_id: BIRD-SQL standard — database identifier, must match folder name (e.g. db-6)
_field_definitions.question_id: BIRD-SQL standard — unique integer per query within this database (1–30)
_field_definitions.question: BIRD-SQL standard — natural-language question the agent receives as input prompt
_field_definitions.SQL: BIRD-SQL standard — golden SQL solution the agent must learn to generate
_field_definitions.evidence: BIRD-SQL standard — chain-of-thought (COT) reasoning the agent uses to bridge the question to the SQL; maps to external_knowledge in LiveSQLBench
_field_definitions.difficulty: BIRD-SQL standard — simple | moderate | challenging; controls curriculum distribution
_field_definitions.query_category: Training extension — SQL pattern label for curriculum coverage (aggregation, join, window/self-join, subquery/cte, filtering/lookup, date-arithmetic, aggregation/ranking)
_field_definitions.tables_used: Training extension — ground-truth table list for schema-linking evaluation
_field_definitions.schema_context: Training extension — per-query schema subset the agent sees at inference time; simulates real-world partial-schema retrieval
_field_definitions.expected_output: Training extension — execution result for reward-model verification (EX metric); stringified 2D array matching SELECT output

question: What is the average length of stay for patients admitted with cardiac conditions in Q4 2024?
SQL:
SELECT AVG(JULIANDAY(discharge_date) - JULIANDAY(admit_date)) AS avg_los
FROM patients p
JOIN diagnoses d ON p.patient_id = d.patient_id
WHERE d.icd_code LIKE 'I%'
  AND p.admit_date BETWEEN '2024-10-01' AND '2024-12-31';
evidence: Length of stay is calculated as discharge_date minus admit_date in days. Cardiac conditions are identified by ICD-10 codes starting with 'I' (diseases of the circulatory system). Q4 2024 refers to October 1 through December 31, 2024.

patients.patient_id: INTEGER PRIMARY KEY — unique patient identifier
patients.admit_date: DATE — date of hospital admission, e.g. '2024-10-15'
patients.discharge_date: DATE — date of hospital discharge, e.g. '2024-10-22'

diagnoses.diagnosis_id: INTEGER PRIMARY KEY — unique diagnosis record
diagnoses.icd_code: VARCHAR(10) — ICD-10 code, e.g. 'I21.0' = acute ST-elevation MI

question: Which department had the highest number of readmissions within 30 days during 2024?
SQL:
WITH readmissions AS (
  SELECT
    p1.department,
    p1.patient_id,
    p1.discharge_date AS first_discharge,
    MIN(p2.admit_date) AS readmit_date
  FROM patients p1
  JOIN patients p2
    ON p1.patient_id = p2.patient_id
    AND p2.admit_date > p1.discharge_date
    AND p2.admit_date <= DATE(p1.discharge_date, '+30 days')
  WHERE p1.discharge_date BETWEEN '2024-01-01' AND '2024-12-31'
  GROUP BY p1.department, p1.patient_id, p1.discharge_date
)
SELECT department, COUNT(*) AS readmission_count
FROM readmissions
GROUP BY department
ORDER BY readmission_count DESC
LIMIT 1;
evidence: A readmission is defined as a new admission for the same patient_id within 30 days of a prior discharge_date. The 30-day window is calculated using DATE(discharge_date, '+30 days') in SQLite. Only index admissions with discharge dates in 2024 are counted.

patients.patient_id: INTEGER — unique patient identifier; same patient can have multiple rows (one per visit)

question: List the top 5 physicians by total billed amount for outpatient visits in 2024.
SQL:
SELECT
  ph.physician_name,
  SUM(b.amount) AS total_billed
FROM billing b
JOIN visits v ON b.visit_id = v.visit_id
JOIN physicians ph ON v.physician_id = ph.physician_id
WHERE v.visit_type = 'outpatient'
  AND v.visit_date BETWEEN '2024-01-01' AND '2024-12-31'
GROUP BY ph.physician_name
ORDER BY total_billed DESC
LIMIT 5;
evidence: Outpatient visits are identified by visit_type = 'outpatient'. Total billed amount is the SUM of billing.amount for all line items associated with a visit. Physicians are linked through visits.physician_id → physicians.physician_id.
